data.sentence: Thank you for calling Aegis Cloud Security support, this is Elena Vasquez — how can I help?
Hi Elena, it's Grace Yoon from Northstar Pharma. We spoke in March during the Detect outage, and, um, I'm back, unfortunately.
Hi Grace, I remember. I'm sorry to hear something's wrong — what's happening?
We're trying to export our HIPAA compliance report from Comply v2 and it fails every time at about ninety percent.
We get an error that says export job terminated, code 5023, and then nothing — no file, not even a partial file.
Okay. Is this the PDF export or the auditor package export?
The auditor package. The PDF works, but our auditors specifically asked for the package with the evidence attachments.
And roughly how large is your evidence library — do you know how many artifacts are attached?
I'd guess around six thousand, we pull in a lot of access review screenshots and change tickets.
Let me pull up your tenant logs while we talk. Can you give me the time of the last failed attempt?
About twenty minutes ago, so around six-fifteen your time.
Got it, I can see three failed jobs today and two yesterday, all terminated at the packaging step.
Elena, I need to be honest about the timing here. Our HIPAA audit fieldwork starts Monday.
And our renewal is in June, and after March my CISO already has SentinelShield on the shortlist. This can't be another fire drill.
Understood, and I don't want this to become one. I'm bringing in my team lead Priya, who has worked the Comply v2 export issues.
Hi Grace, Priya here. I've just looked at the job — it's hitting the two-gigabyte package limit that shipped with v2.
Your attachments come to about two point four gigabytes, and right now the job fails instead of splitting the package, which is a bug on our side.
So it's not something we did.
No, not at all. The limit should trigger a split into multiple volumes and it doesn't. We've seen it with two other large tenants.
Okay. What can we do before Monday?
Two options. I can run the export from our side with the split flag enabled, which produces three volumes your auditors can open normally.
Or you can filter the export by control family and run it in three parts yourself, but that's more work for your team.
I'd rather you run it. Will the auditors see anything different?
The content and the hashes are identical, it's just split across files. I'll include a manifest so they can verify nothing is missing.
Okay, that I can work with.
I'm also marking the case P1 given the audit date, and I'll get you an ETA on the permanent fix from engineering.
I appreciate that. I'll be blunt though — it's frustrating that the feature we were sold as the fix for our compliance pain breaks on our first real audit.
That's completely fair, and I'll make sure your account team hears it directly, not just through the ticket.
Please do. Maria has been good about following up, I'd like her in the loop.
I'll copy Maria Santos on the case summary today.
Grace, I can have the split package to you by end of day tomorrow, Pacific. Does that give you enough time to review before Monday?
Yes, if it's tomorrow. Can you send it through the secure share rather than email?
Yes, it'll go through the secure portal, and I'll send you a notification with the manifest attached.
Okay. And I'll need a short write-up on the cause — the auditors may ask why the package came in volumes.
We'll include a one-page note explaining the split and confirming data integrity.
Alright. Thank you both, really. Let's just get through Monday.
We will. I'll check in with you tomorrow afternoon as soon as the package is ready.
